title: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Q-Learning

methods.one_paragraph_description: Learns a state value function V by expectile regression (expectile tau) on Q(s,a) over dataset actions only, and a Q function by TD regression toward r + gamma V(s'), never querying Q at out-of-dataset actions. Uses clipped double Q (min of two Q nets) with soft target updates. The policy is extracted separately with advantage-weighted regression, weights exp(beta*(Q-V)) clipped at 100.
methods.conventional_lineage_hint: offline RL ('a new offline RL algorithm that avoids ever querying values of unseen actions'; builds on 'approximate dynamic programming methods')

expectile_tau.quote: We use τ = 0.9 and β = 10.0 for Ant Maze tasks and τ = 0.7 and β = 3.0 for MuJoCo locomotion tasks.

inverse_temperature_beta.quote: We use τ = 0.9 and β = 10.0 for Ant Maze tasks and τ = 0.7 and β = 3.0 for MuJoCo locomotion tasks.

optimizer.quote: We use Adam opti- mizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with a learning rate 3 · 10−4

learning_rate.quote: We use Adam opti- mizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with a learning rate 3 · 10−4 and 2 layer MLP with ReLU activations and 256 hidden units for all networks.

network.value: 2-layer MLP, 256 hidden units, ReLU, all networks
network.quote: 2 layer MLP with ReLU activations and 256 hidden units for all networks

actor_lr_schedule.quote: We use cosine schedule for the actor learning rate.

policy_parameterization.quote: We param- eterize the policy as a Gaussian distribution with a state-independent standard deviation.

target_update_rate.quote: We update the target network with soft updates with parameter α = 0.005.

advantage_weight_clip.quote: following Brandfonbrener et al. (2021) we clip exponentiated advantages to (−∞, 100].

reward_normalization.value: divide by (best - worst trajectory return) in dataset
reward_normalization.quote: We standardize MuJoCo locomotion task rewards by dividing by the difference of re- turns of the best and worst trajectories in each dataset.

num_q_networks.quote: we use a version of clipped double Q-learning (Fujimoto et al., 2018), taking a minimum of two Q-functions for V -function and policy updates.

gradient_steps.value: 1M updates (stated in runtime discussion; not explicitly tied to Table 1)
gradient_steps.quote: we can perform 1M updates on one GTX1080 GPU in less than 20 minutes.

evaluation_protocol.quote: For the MuJoCo locomotion tasks, we average mean returns overs 10 eval- uation trajectories and 10 random seeds.

dataset_version.quote: We use the “-v2” environments for all methods to ensure a fair comparison
dataset_version.location: Section 5.2 (dataset names in Table 1 end in -v2)
